## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/tooltip ``` Optionally wrap the app in `TooltipProvider` once to set one delay for every tooltip; Base UI does not require it. These examples also use `@cadence/button`; the icon example uses `lucide-react`. **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | tooltip | `@components/cadence/tooltip/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/tooltip.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: tooltip](https://cadence.dev/r/tooltip.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all nine target files, keeping `tooltip/index.tsx` and the shared `lib/` directory in the same `cadence/` tree. Preserve relative imports and the sources' `"use client"` directives. Copy every file in the motion, utilities and provider payloads, including helpers not imported by Tooltip directly. The provider files and `motion` package are required imports even without the optional `CadenceProvider` wrapper. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. Include the Cadence easing and motion-scale tokens used by the popup classes. No additional item-specific CSS or external asset is required. Full fades and scales the label from its anchor; reduced keeps opacity only; none removes transitions and hidden entry/exit styles. The portalled popup resolves its own mode and token clock. Standalone components follow the system motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested full still respects system reduced motion. [Button](https://cadence.dev/components/button#installation) is used by Usage, the top specimen and every body example. Copy its complete Manual setup, including its npm dependencies and shared files. Usage and the top specimen also import an icon: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` Logical sides and RTL imports Base UI `DirectionProvider` from the already required `@base-ui/react` package. Explicit motion scopes uses the included Cadence provider. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, Controlled needs a caller client module for its state and event handlers. The other examples and top specimen contain serializable JSX and element-valued `render` props, so they can be composed in synchronous Server Components. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`, `className(state)` or `style(state)` also need a caller client boundary. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require one. Keep the installed client directives and the snippets' existing directives when copying them unchanged. Place `TooltipTrigger` and `TooltipContent` within the same `Tooltip` root. Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled opening, or `open` / `onOpenChange` for caller control. External opening needs a unique `triggerId` matching the trigger's `id`, as in Controlled, to keep the popup anchored. The trigger renders a button by default; `render={ Finish the required fields first ); } ``` ## Controlled The external Show shortcut action owns open state. A unique triggerId anchors that update to Keyboard help; normal focus, hover, and Escape still report changes through onOpenChange. The popup carries only explanatory text. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId, useState } from "react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip"; export function ControlledTooltip() { const id = useId(); const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); return (
}> Keyboard help Press ⌘K to search
); } ``` ## Explicit motion scopes These explicit overrides show none from insertion and full restored within that none scope, subject to OS reduction. Other examples inherit the site header. The tooltip delay is interaction timing and is independent of its motion mode. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip"; export function TooltipMotionScopes() { return (
}>Open without motion Immediate tooltip }>Open nested full The OS preference still wins
); } ``` ## When to use - An icon-only control whose meaning is not obvious from the icon alone. - The full value behind a truncated label, or a keyboard shortcut next to an action. - A hint that helps the first use of a dense control and is useless once learned. ## When not to use - Anything the user must read to act: a tooltip disappears on scroll, touch, and Escape. If the content matters, put it on the page or in a `popover`. - Interactive content. A tooltip cannot hold a button or a link; use `popover`. - The accessible name of a button that already has text. Two labels that disagree is worse than one. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `TooltipProvider` | `delay` | Optional. One delay for every tooltip inside. | | `Tooltip` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `triggerId`, `disabled` | Base UI root; `triggerId` anchors external open updates. | | `TooltipTrigger` | native button props, `render`, `delay`, `closeDelay`, `disabled` | Hover/focus target; carries `aria-describedby`. Trigger `disabled` suppresses the hint; disable the rendered Button separately to block its action. | | `TooltipContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, popup, and arrow. `side` defaults to `top`, `sideOffset` to `4`. | ## Motion contract Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | label `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes | | exit | label `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes | | reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the label appears on the first frame | – | – | A tooltip is small enough that `duration.fast` is already at the edge of readable: nothing here waits for an exit to finish. The arrow is part of the popup and moves with it, so it is never animated separately. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus shows the label; leaving hides it. | | Escape | Hides the label and leaves focus on the trigger. | | Enter / Space | Activates the trigger. The tooltip does not swallow the press. | Keyboard focus provides an additional route to the same explanation. Keep essential instructions visible on the page, including for touch users. ## Accessibility - Base UI's own tooltip adds neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-describedby`; Cadence wires both. The trigger points at the popup only while it is open — a closed popup would otherwise leave a dangling id, which axe reports — and the popup is `role="tooltip"`. - The tooltip must not be the only name of a control. Give an icon button a real `aria-label`; the tooltip is the extra sentence, not the name. - Text stays readable in both themes: `bg-foreground` / `text-background` invert, so the label keeps contrast against whatever surface it floats over. - Escape dismisses it without moving focus, so a tooltip never traps a keyboard user. ## Responsive behavior The label is `w-fit` with a `max-w-xs` cap and wraps at word boundaries (`text-balance`) instead of running off screen. Base UI flips the side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it. ## Performance - The popup tree is mounted only while the label is open; a page can carry dozens of tooltips without paying for them all. - Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no measuring loop, no JavaScript animation. Hover is not a state the component polls. ## Notes for AI - Use a tooltip to name or explain a control, never to deliver information the user needs to proceed. - Do not put a link, button, or form inside it; use `popover`. - Give every icon-only trigger an `aria-label`: the tooltip complements the name, it does not replace it.
